name_reason: Compliant with global naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix + battle domain (core battle table) + miss_indicator purpose + sprite_ids reflects the array-of-ids data type. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix matching its own or any data address). Accurately describes the 4 text-glyph sprite ids for the MISS/dodge floating indicator.
purpose: The 4 text-glyph sprite ids for the "MISS"/dodge (閃避) floating combat indicator, one sprite id per the 4 indicator frames enqueued above the dodging target.
logic_summary: Sole reader fd2_show_miss_indicator @ 0x1E1DC loads all 4 bytes at 0x5204A as one dword into a stack scratch (MOV EAX,[0x5204A]; MOV [ESP],EAX), then in a 4-iteration loop reads the dword copy byte-by-byte (MOV BL,byte ptr [ESP+char_iter]) and enqueues each byte as a sprite id into the floating-text sprite-id queue (one per frame). The dword load is just a bulk copy; the data is semantically a 4-element byte array. Read-only (single READ xref, no writers).
element_semantics: Each element is a uint8 text-glyph sprite id used for one frame of the MISS/dodge floating indicator. Values {0x74, 0x75, 0x76, 0x76} (verified against memory at 0x5204A).
notes: No code unit / no data type is defined at 0x5204A: the label sits inside the reader function's code region as an embedded constant literal (.object2). Therefore there is no separate data plate to update; the reader function fd2_show_miss_indicator already documents this literal accurately at the function level, and per the per-symbol scope rule the reader's plate is not this symbol's plate, so ghidra_plate_action=none. The existing btltab.c comment block (lines 425-445) and the globals.h extern declaration (line 145) are accurate, ASCII-clean, and matched exactly to disasm/memory; comment kept unchanged, so btltab.c is not modified. 閃避 retained as a domain proper noun (dodge/evade) per ASCII-only-except-CJK-proper-nouns rule.
